source.question: Which wells need attention right now, and why? Forecast the next 12 months of oil for the well that needs it most.

note: Fair: undeclared 81 (days since the gauge died), 3% and 80% written in claims.

submission.summary: F-12 needs attention most: it is on alarm with a dead downhole gauge and water taking capacity. F-14 is on caution with rising water cut. Field totals have not exceeded the platform’s design limits for liquid, oil or water cut. Forecast for F-12 for the next 12 months suggests about 359 thousand Sm3 oil, but the fit is poor so uncertainty is high.

findings.claim: F-12 needs attention most: alarm level at 1 551 Sm3/d oil with 69% water cut, downhole gauge dead since 2010-10-12 (81 days, 123 258 Sm3 oil without pressure data).
findings.detail: field_screen as_of 2010-12-31: F-12 oil_rate 1551 Sm3/d, water_cut 0.6939, uptime 0.9846, level alarm; dead_gauge since 2010-10-12, 81 days, 123258 Sm3. detect_events gauge_failure bhp_bar 0 on 81 days 2010-10-12 to 2010-12-31. Field_screen 90-day oil change -16.5%.

findings.claim: F-12’s oil rate fell 55% around 2010-05-02 to 1 888 Sm3/d, a gradual shift with water cut rising from 3% to 57% and liquid holding while choke narrowed.
findings.detail: detect_events oil regime_change around 2010-05-02: weekly mean 4207 -> 1888 Sm3/d (-55.12%), across 4 weeks 3196 -> 2538 (-20.59%). Water_cut regime 2010-02-28: 0.0339 -> 0.5701. Water_cut >5% 2009-10-31, >50% 2010-06-04. Waterflood by_year 2009: liquid 4740 Sm3/d choke 59.88% water_cut 0.0229 oil 1522541; 2010: liquid 5130 Sm3/d choke 53.17% water_cut 0.5711 oil 873828. Field voidage replacement_ratio 2010 1.08 (reservoir conditions) indicating injection kept pace.

findings.claim: F-14 is on caution: oil rate 2 175 Sm3/d with 61% water cut, 34% lower around 2010-01-10, a gradual change.
findings.detail: field_screen F-14 oil_rate 2175, water_cut 0.6112, shift_down 2010-01-10 weekly mean 3616 -> 2397 (-33.69%), across 2892 -> 2657 (-8.13%). Thresholds: >5% 2009-06-21, >50% 2010-04-05. Waterflood by_year 2009 liquid 4275 choke 38.09 water_cut 0.07828; 2010 liquid 5439 choke 59.11 water_cut 0.5536.

findings.claim: Field totals have not exceeded design: liquid peaked at 10 826 Sm3/d versus 13 000 capacity and water cut peaked at 67% versus 80% design.
findings.detail: field_vs_design: liquid max 10826 in 2010-06 (0 months >=13000), oil max 8924 in 2008-12 (0 months >=9000), water_cut max 0.6715 in 2010-12 (0 months >=0.80), water handling max 7193 vs 10400. Water injection capacity 16000 exceeded in 3 months, max 17206 in 2008-12. Rates per calendar day.

findings.claim: Forecast for F-12 for next 12 months (2011-01-01 to 2011-12-31) is 359 007 Sm3 P50 with calibrated band 324 192 to 469 712 Sm3.
findings.detail: forecast_production fit from 2010-05-02 to 2010-12-31: harmonic qi 2628 di 1.31 b 1.0 r2_log 0.6881 rmse_log 0.1244 n 227 uptime 0.9246. Cumulative P50 359007 P90 339803 P10 374234 bootstrap; calibrated_band P90 324192 P10 469712 from 5 past forecasts median_abs_error 0.0961. Monthly P50 rates 1363 -> 841 Sm3/producing_day. p50_by_model exponential 302158 harmonic/hyperbolic 359007. WARNING poor fit r2_log <0.7.

result.no_trend: too few months with WOR >= 1 (water cut 0.5) to fit a trend: 7, need 12
result.notes: WOR = water/oil by month; the trend is log10(WOR) against cumulative oil, fitted on up to 36 recent months with WOR >= 1. field_voidage: replacement_ratio is injection over voidage at reservoir conditions (Bo 1.385 m3/Sm3 from PUD p.20, low/high with Bo 1.5/1.27; Bw 1; above the bubble point, so no free gas); surface_ratio is the same in surface volumes, which overstates replacement.

result.scope: whole field, all producers and injectors summed per day, then per month
result.plan_source: Plan for utbygging og drift av Volve (PUD, plan for development and operation), page 23, Table 4.3

water_sm3_per_day.limit: field water handling (derived: liquid capacity x maximum water cut)

result.plan_end_quote: Kumulativ oljeproduksjon inntil minimum økonomisk rate på 2.100 Sm3 /d (gitt Volve oljepris på 18,7 USD/fat) nås er 11,4 MSm3
result.note: These are field and platform limits (PUD p.35 lists the same platform capacities); compare them with field totals, never one well. The maximum water cut is a share at full liquid rate: the water the platform can handle is liquid capacity x maximum water cut (water_sm3_per_day). The field reaching that share at a lower liquid rate means it ran at the design water cut, not over its water capacity. Rates are per calendar day of each month.
